  "summary": "The packet describes a careful three-day effort with honest evaluation caveats; the executor-resolver executability fix and the card-swap guard are the strongest pieces because they align routing checks with the file the executor actually runs and close a real reply-text override path. The main risks are in the catalog-mutating tooling: decisions that were made manually during the run (exclude Bioconductor rows, do not apply moves into 'general') are not enforced in the apply/verify code, so a future full run can re-introduce the exact wrong catalog edits. The step-8a input-kind scoring is a reasonable first pass but the +3 'exactly the right input kind' branch is logically an overlap check, not exact compatibility. Evaluation evidence is small and partly pre-registered after the before-arm, but the packet mostly does not over-claim the broad routing numbers. The DAG planner has one brittle identity-mapping pattern that should be cleaned up.",

      "claim": "The documented decision to apply the false-claim audit only to BioMate-authored annotations is not enforced by the tool; a future run of verify+apply over the full verified file would overwrite Bioconductor annotations with the very mis-confirmations the packet says they excluded.",

Applied only to BioMate-authored annotations (19 rows)'. Code: `n += conn.execute(\"UPDATE workflows SET annotation = ? WHERE name = ? AND annotation = ?\", (cleaned(...), v[\"name\"], v[\"annotation\"])).rowcount` — no source predicate or source-containing verified-row guard.",

Print per-source update counts and fail closed when a source is not in the allowlist.",

      "depends_on_unseen": false
    },
    {
      "id": "F2",
      "severity": "major",
      "area": "catalog mutation tooling",
      "location": "scripts/routing_eval/verify_domain_retag.py",
      "claim": "The verifier emits SQL for every two-model-agreed change, including moves into `general`, despite the packet stating those were not applied; the exclusion is manual and not in the code.",
      "evidence": "Packet §2.F.1: 'moves into `general` not applied'. Script: `ok = [o for o in out if o[\"agreed\"]]` followed by writing `UPDATE workflows SET domain = ...` for every `o` in `ok`; there is no `o[\"proposed_domain\"] != \"general\"` filter.",
      "suggested_fix": "Filter the emitted SQL to exclude `proposed_domain == 'general'` (or make it an explicit opt-in flag), so the script's default behavior matches the documented, safer rule.",
      "confidence": "high",
      "depends_on_unseen": false
    },
    {
      "id": "F3",
      "severity": "minor",
      "area": "routing scoring",
      "location": "backend/lib/galaxy/ai/unified_workflow_search.py:_calculate_score step 8a",
      "claim": "The +3 'exactly the right input kind' branch is actually an any-overlap bonus; for workflows that accept multiple required primary inputs, a user with only one overlapping kind gets credited and the raw-vs-processed mismatch check may be bypassed.",
      "evidence": "`if user_kinds & input_kinds: score += 3.0  # user has exactly the right input kind` — it does not require that all necessary workflow kinds are present, only that at least one is.",
      "suggested_fix": "Either remove the +3 bonus and rely on the mismatch penalty, or compute coverage over the workflow's required raw/processed/other kinds; be explicit that `input_kinds` is interpreted as accepted alternatives rather than co-required inputs.",
      "confidence": "medium",
      "depends_on_unseen": false
    },
    {
      "id": "F4",
      "severity": "minor",
      "area": "DAG planning",
      "location": "backend/lib/galaxy/ai/decomposed_dag.py:plan_dag_from_tasks",
      "claim": "The task-to-index map uses Python's built-in `id(t)` on task dicts instead of the task's explicit `id` field; if `build_dag_plan` ever passes copied/reconstructed task dicts, resolution silently returns None and the plan can fall back to per-intent behavior for the wrong reason.",
      "evidence": "`_idx = {id(t): i for i, t in enumerate(tasks)}` and `build_dag_plan(tasks, lambda t: resolved.get(_idx.get(id(t))), ...)` — the task schema already has a stable `id` field.",
      "suggested_fix": "Use `_idx = {t.get(\"id\") or f\"task_{i+1}\": i for i, t in enumerate(tasks)}` and `resolved.get(_idx.get(t.get(\"id\") or ...))`, or pass the index directly to an explicit resolver.",
      "confidence": "low",
      "depends_on_unseen": true
    },
    {
      "id": "F5",
      "severity": "minor",
      "area": "chat routing / execution mode",
      "location": "frontend/server/galaxy-assistant.ts direct-compute override",
      "claim": "The classifier-driven `direct_compute` override does not exclude requests where the user asks for code itself, while the codebase already has `wantsCodeItself()` for that distinction; a 'write Python code to summarize my attached table' request can be forced into executing code rather than returning code.",
      "evidence": "`const _directCompute = (intent as any).execution === 'direct_compute' && hasComputableData(message); if (actions.needsWorkflowGeneration && (... || _directCompute)) { actions.needsWorkflowGeneration = false; ... }` — no `!wantsCodeItself(message)` guard, although `wantsCodeItself` is defined in the same file.",
      "suggested_fix": "Add `&& !wantsCodeItself(message)` to `_directCompute` or to the overall direct-compute override condition.",
      "confidence": "medium",
      "depends_on_unseen": false
    },

      "severity": "minor",
      "area": "domain retag CLI",
      "location": "backend/lib/galaxy/ai/chain_composer/domain_reclassifier.py:reclassify",
      "claim": "`--canonical` without `--all-domains` still only audits `domain='general'`, which makes the flag easy to misuse and inconsistent with its closed-list purpose; the actual canonical run required both flags, but the tool does not enforce or document that.",
      "evidence": "SQL: `\"FROM workflows WHERE executable=1 \" + (\"\" if all_domains else \"AND domain='general' \")`; `--canonical` help says only `closed list = router's CANONICAL_DOMAINS + general + current tag`.",
      "suggested_fix": "Make `--canonical` imply `all_domains=True`, or raise a parser error if `--canonical` is used without `--all-domains`, so a partial audit cannot be run accidentally.",
      "confidence": "high",
      "depends_on_unseen": false
    },
    {
      "id": "F7",
      "severity": "minor",
      "area": "annotation audit tooling",
      "location": "backend/lib/galaxy/ai/chain_composer/annotation_claim_audit.py:_rows",
      "claim": "The annotation-audit row query assumes the `input_kinds` column already exists; if run on an older DB or before the input-kinds pass, it fails at SQL level rather than degrading gracefully.",

      "suggested_fix": "Check `PRAGMA table_info(workflows)` and substitute `'[]'` when the column is absent, or make the prerequisite explicit in the CLI help and fail with a clear error before SQL execution.",
      "confidence": "high",
      "depends_on_unseen": false
    }

  "keep": [
    "The executor-resolver executability fix (`_resolve_execution_nf`) is right: routing should judge the actual file the executor runs, not the display stub; this matches the resolver-order fix described in the packet.",
    "The Step 6c/6c-2 card-swap guard limiting swaps to search candidates and input-compatible targets is a real safety improvement; text-driven swaps were a clear failure mode.",
    "The order-only DAG fallback is conservative: it preserves dependency order without fabricating typed data connections and surfaces `unwired_dependencies` to the user.",
    "Marking the keyword fallback as `degraded` instead of silently scoring is the correct evaluation-facing behavior; so is the one LLM fallback-chain attempt before that heuristic.",
    "The manual test instructions and pre-sync DB checks are well specified and should be kept; they are appropriate for a non-version-controlled catalog."
  ],
  "answers": {
    "q1": "The step-8a design is acceptable as a lightweight first pass, but a fixed −25 is brittle and the exact-compat bonus is mis-specified. The biggest failure modes are: (1) misleading mentions — the regex side observes words, not actual possession, so 'do I need to convert my proteinGroups.txt back to mzML?' can produce both raw_spectra and protein_table and then no mismatch; (2) users with multiple data kinds are treated by overlap rather than per-workflow requirements; (3) multi-input workflows get an +3 overlap bonus while still missing another required input; (4) LLM labels carry ~4% disagreement and duplicate names share one label. A hard filter is too strong until labels/query detection improve and would have blocked rows where both kinds are present. I would keep it as a strong penalty, remove or rename the +3 exact bonus, and add an explicit 'ask the user' path when the requested data kind is ambiguous and the top-ranked workflow has an input-kind mismatch.",
    "q2": "Text should not blindly override the backend card. The backend ranking plus `_llm_verify_routing` should decide the executable card; the reply is generated after the decision and can hallucinate workflow names. The safest precedence is backend card > LLM verify > reply text, where reply text is only allowed to trigger a constrained re-search or re-verification over the original candidates. A random `nf-core/*` mentioned in prose should never become the card unless it is already in the search candidate set and passes the same compatibility checks. The current candidate+input_compatible guard is a good step, but I would strengthen it by making any conflict log a visible 'why I kept the workflow' note rather than silently ignoring the text.",
    "q3": "The prompts and guarded SQL are thoughtfully designed, and the two-model disagreement step is better than a single LLM pass. But 'two LLMs agree' is not sufficient evidence to edit a production catalog with no version control: the two models can share prompt-induced bias, and the verifier prompt explicitly says the description may be incomplete and asks the model to rely on world knowledge, which produced the Bioconductor wrong confirmations. Before repeated use I would add: per-source allowlists enforced in code (not only in the run narrative), a write-ahead DB snapshot and automatic generated diff, a `provenance` table recording each catalog edit with the proposal/verifier JSON, human sign-off for claim removals on upstream-sourced annotations, and canary rows to detect over-aggressive future passes.",
    "q4": "The evidence is not enough to support broad conclusions, but it is probably enough to keep the changes deployed as an experiment with a fast rollback path. The 20×2 dev A/B is very small, the strict criterion was added after the before-arm (even if before after-arms), and several control flips are within LLM stochastic noise. The offline harness measures only the scorer and was already able to pass the MaxQuant row while production failed, so offline numbers should not be used as a deployment gate. The current-arm strict improvement from 4/8 to 5/8 is not statistically meaningful, and the claim that G 'fixed' E should be phrased as one observed rep, not a verified fix. A v2 query set with corrected criteria, more reps, blind criteria, and production-component inclusion should be built before reusing these numbers in a decision.",
    "q5": "The FTS term should not be made to dominate the final score. Better options: keep FTS/BM25 for candidate retrieval and truncation, then feed it to a reranker as a log-scaled or percentile feature alongside domain/input-kind/tags; learn coefficient weights on a held-out routing set; or use a pointwise or pairwise reranking model with lexical, source, domain, and input-kind features. A fixed hand-set penalty for one semantic signal will interact unpredictably with lexical score across query types. If a learned model is too expensive, a calibrated heuristic with bounded components and a residual FTS tie-breaker is safer than the current absolute BM25 × 1.5 dominance.",
    "q6": "Real code-level issues found in this review: F1 (annotation audit apply lacks the documented Bioconductor/BioMate source guard), F2 (domain retag verifier does not exclude moves into `general`), F3 (input-kind +3 bonus is overlap, not exact compatibility), F4 (`plan_dag_from_tasks` uses `id(t)` instead of the task id field), F5 (`direct_compute` override ignores `wantsCodeItself`), F6 (`--canonical` without `--all-domains` silently audits only `domain='general'`), and F7 (annotation audit assumes `input_kinds` exists). None is an obvious Python 3.9 incompatibility in the shown code, but the concurrent-catalog-write risk remains high because the catalog is still not version-controlled."
  }
}
